steps.name: resolve
steps.script:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail
lookup_result() {
  # lookup_result <pipelineTask> <result-name> - empty when the TaskRun or result doesn't exist.
  kubectl get taskrun -n "${APP_NAMESPACE}" \
    -l "tekton.dev/pipelineRun=${PIPELINE_RUN_NAME},tekton.dev/pipelineTask=$1" \
    -o jsonpath="{.items[0].status.results[?(@.name==\"$2\")].value}" 2>/dev/null || true
}

IMAGE_REF="${IMAGE_REF_PARAM}"
if [[ -z "${IMAGE_REF}" && -n "${IMAGE_REF_FROM_TASK}" ]]; then
  IMAGE_REF="$(lookup_result "${IMAGE_REF_FROM_TASK}" image-ref)"
  echo "image-ref from ${IMAGE_REF_FROM_TASK}'s TaskRun result: '${IMAGE_REF}'"
fi

CONFIG_JSON="${CONFIG_JSON_PARAM}"
if [[ -n "${CONFIG_JSON_FROM_TASK}" ]]; then
  looked_up="$(lookup_result "${CONFIG_JSON_FROM_TASK}" config-json)"
  if [[ -n "${looked_up}" ]] && jq -e . <<<"${looked_up}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    CONFIG_JSON="${looked_up}"
  else
    echo "no usable config-json result on ${CONFIG_JSON_FROM_TASK}'s TaskRun (it failed or never ran) - notifications fall back to the config-json param" >&2
  fi
fi
[[ -z "${CONFIG_JSON}" ]] && CONFIG_JSON='{}'

# ${IMAGE_REF} token substitution via jq's own string ops, never shell
# interpolation into JSON text, so a reference containing a quote can't break it.
CONTENT="$(jq -c --arg img "${IMAGE_REF}" \
  'walk(if type == "string" then gsub("\\$\\{IMAGE_REF\\}"; $img) else . end)' \
  <<<"${CONTENT_TEMPLATE}" 2>/dev/null || echo "${CONTENT_TEMPLATE}")"

printf '%s' "${IMAGE_REF}" > "/tekton/steps/step-resolve/results/image-ref"
printf '%s' "${CONFIG_JSON}" | base64 -w0 > "/tekton/steps/step-resolve/results/config-json-b64"
printf '%s' "${CONTENT}" | base64 -w0 > "/tekton/steps/step-resolve/results/subject-content-json-b64"

steps.name: notify-slack
steps.script:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
CFG="${CONFIG_JSON}"
if [[ -n "${CONFIG_JSON_B64}" ]]; then
  CFG="$(base64 -d <<<"${CONFIG_JSON_B64}")"
fi
ENABLED="$(jq -r '.notifications.slack.enabled // false' <<< "${CFG}")"
if [[ "${ENABLED}" != "true" ]]; then
  echo "slack notifications disabled in cicd.yaml, skipping"
  exit 0
fi
CHANNEL="$(jq -r '.notifications.slack.channel // empty' <<< "${CFG}")"
WEBHOOK_URL="$(cat /var/run/secrets/platform/slack-webhook-url 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ -z "${WEBHOOK_URL}" ]]; then
  echo "warn: notifications.slack.enabled=true but no slack-webhook-url secret is mounted for this Application - skipping, not failing the pipeline" >&2
  exit 0
fi

# docs/design-language.md: blue accent, muted red + a single ⚠ only on failure -
# not a stoplight, not a per-stage icon.
case "${STAGE_NAME}" in
  build) STAGE_DISPLAY="Build" ;;
  test) STAGE_DISPLAY="Test" ;;
  deploy) STAGE_DISPLAY="Deploy" ;;
  release) STAGE_DISPLAY="Release" ;;
  deploying) STAGE_DISPLAY="Deploying" ;;
  release-outcome) STAGE_DISPLAY="Release" ;;
  *) STAGE_DISPLAY="${STAGE_NAME}" ;;
esac
# Syncing (the new release-progress-notify mid-flow stage) is routine, not a
# failure - without this it'd render red with the ⚠ failure marker.
if [[ "${STATUS}" == "Succeeded" || "${STATUS}" == "Completed" || "${STATUS}" == "Syncing" ]]; then
  COLOR="#2563EB"
else
  COLOR="#B91C1C"
fi

# Same per-stage wording fix as notify-backstage.yaml's identical switch (see
# that Task's own 2026-09-14 comment for the full reasoning) - the blind
# "${STAGE_DISPLAY} ${STATUS}" concatenation misrepresents release's three
# lifecycle notification points. Unlike notify-backstage.yaml's title (Tower's
# Recent Activity panel is already scoped to one app), APP_NAME stays here -
# #all-idp-lab is a shared channel across every app, so "Release triggered for
# prod" alone would be ambiguous about whose prod.
case "${STAGE_NAME}" in
  release)
    if [[ "${STATUS}" == "Succeeded" || "${STATUS}" == "Completed" ]]; then
      HEADER_TEXT="${APP_NAME} · Release triggered for ${ENV_NAME}"
    else
      HEADER_TEXT="⚠ ${APP_NAME} · Release trigger failed for ${ENV_NAME}"
    fi
    ;;
  deploying) HEADER_TEXT="${APP_NAME} · Deploying release to ${ENV_NAME}" ;;
  release-outcome)
    if [[ "${STATUS}" == "Succeeded" || "${STATUS}" == "Completed" ]]; then
      HEADER_TEXT="${APP_NAME} · Release succeeded in ${ENV_NAME}"
    else
      HEADER_TEXT="⚠ ${APP_NAME} · Release failed in ${ENV_NAME}"
    fi
    ;;
  *)
    if [[ "${STATUS}" == "Succeeded" || "${STATUS}" == "Completed" ]]; then
      HEADER_TEXT="${APP_NAME} · ${STAGE_DISPLAY} ${STATUS}"
    else
      HEADER_TEXT="⚠ ${APP_NAME} · ${STAGE_DISPLAY} ${STATUS}"
    fi
    ;;
esac

# 12-char SHA for display only (matches sast-scan.yaml/image-scan.yaml) -
# intentionally independent of build-image.yaml's own 7-char image-tag SHA.
REPO_SHORT="$(echo "${GIT_URL}" | sed -E 's#https?://github\.com/([^/]+)/([^/.]+).*#\1/\2#')"
SHORT_SHA="${GIT_REVISION:0:12}"
COMMIT_URL="${GIT_URL}/commit/${GIT_REVISION}"

# Tekton Dashboard deep-link (HashRouter route, undocumented but confirmed
# against the installed dashboard's JS bundle). Only resolves when someone has
# the dashboard port-forwarded locally (no ingress/stable URL exists yet) - a
# dead link otherwise costs nothing.
DASHBOARD_URL="http://localhost:9097/#/namespaces/${APP_NAMESPACE}/pipelineruns/${PIPELINE_RUN_NAME}"

# build only - best-effort live lookup of build-image's own result, not a
# Tekton-level $(tasks.build-image.results.image-ref) param reference: Tekton
# skips a finally task entirely if any param references a result from a task
# that failed/didn't run, which would break notification on exactly the failure
# case that matters most. Previously hand-reconstructed a guessed ref (a real
# bug, wrong once build-image started tagging <version>-<sha>) - querying the
# TaskRun result directly reports the exact tag pushed, and comes back empty
# cleanly when build-image never ran or failed.
if [[ -z "${IMAGE_REF}" && "${STAGE_NAME}" == "build" ]]; then
  IMAGE_REF="$(kubectl get taskrun -n "${APP_NAMESPACE}" -l "tekton.dev/pipelineRun=${PIPELINE_RUN_NAME},tekton.dev/pipelineTask=build-image" \
    -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.results[?(@.name=="image-ref")].value}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi

# release only - same reasoning as the build-image lookup above: a
# $(tasks.open-release-pr.results...) reference would skip this notify task
# whenever open-release-pr fails, which is release's most likely failure point.
pr_url="${PR_URL_PARAM}"
if [[ -z "${pr_url}" && "${STAGE_NAME}" == "release" ]]; then
  pr_url="$(kubectl get taskrun -n "${APP_NAMESPACE}" -l "tekton.dev/pipelineRun=${PIPELINE_RUN_NAME},tekton.dev/pipelineTask=open-release-pr" \
    -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.results[?(@.name=="pr-url")].value}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi

# Failure log excerpt - attempted for any non-success status (Cancelled/Timeout
# included), not just "Failed". Needs no new RBAC - pipeline-runner's existing
# Role already covers taskruns/pods/pods-log.
failed_taskrun=""
log_excerpt=""
if [[ "${STATUS}" != "Succeeded" && "${STATUS}" != "Completed" && "${STATUS}" != "Syncing" ]]; then
  failed_taskrun="$(kubectl get taskrun -n "${APP_NAMESPACE}" -l "tekton.dev/pipelineRun=${PIPELINE_RUN_NAME}" -o json \
    | jq -r '[.items[] | select(.status.conditions[0].status == "False")][0].metadata.name // empty')"
  if [[ -n "${failed_taskrun}" ]]; then
    pod_name="$(kubectl get taskrun "${failed_taskrun}" -n "${APP_NAMESPACE}" -o jsonpath='{.status.podName}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ -n "${pod_name}" ]]; then
      log_excerpt="$(kubectl logs "${pod_name}" -n "${APP_NAMESPACE}" --all-containers --tail=30 2>/dev/null | tail -c 1500 || true)"
    fi
  fi
fi

payload="$(jq -n \
  --arg channel "${CHANNEL}" \
  --arg color "${COLOR}" \
  --arg headerText "${HEADER_TEXT}" \
  --arg app "${APP_NAME}" \
  --arg appNamespace "${APP_NAMESPACE}" \
  --arg repoShort "${REPO_SHORT}" \
  --arg repoUrl "${GIT_URL}" \
  --arg shortSha "${SHORT_SHA}" \
  --arg commitUrl "${COMMIT_URL}" \
  --arg image "${IMAGE_REF}" \
  --arg runName "${PIPELINE_RUN_NAME}" \
  --arg dashboardUrl "${DASHBOARD_URL}" \
  --arg envName "${ENV_NAME}" \
  --arg prUrl "${pr_url}" \
  --arg failedTask "${failed_taskrun}" \
  --arg logExcerpt "${log_excerpt}" \
  --arg footer "glidepath · $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
  '
  def field(fieldLabel; fieldValue): {type: "mrkdwn", text: ("*" + fieldLabel + "*\n" + fieldValue)};
  (
    [
      field("App"; $app),
      field("App Namespace"; $appNamespace),
      field("Repo"; "<" + $repoUrl + "|" + $repoShort + ">"),
      field("Commit"; "<" + $commitUrl + "|" + $shortSha + ">")
    ]
    + (if $image != "" then [field("Image"; "`" + $image + "`")] else [] end)
    + (if $envName != "" then [field("Environment"; $envName)] else [] end)
    + [field("Run"; "<" + $dashboardUrl + "|" + $runName + ">")]
    + (if $prUrl != "" then [field("PR"; "<" + $prUrl + "|View PR>")] else [] end)
  ) as $fields
  |
  (
    {
      channel: $channel,
      attachments: [{
        color: $color,
        blocks: (
          [
            {type: "header", text: {type: "plain_text", text: $headerText, emoji: true}},
            {type: "section", fields: $fields}
          ]
          + (if $logExcerpt != "" then [
              {type: "section", text: {type: "mrkdwn", text: ("*Failed task:* `" + $failedTask + "`")}},
              {type: "section", text: {type: "mrkdwn", text: ("```" + $logExcerpt + "```")}}
            ] else [] end)
          + [{type: "context", elements: [{type: "mrkdwn", text: $footer}]}]
        )
      }]
    }
  )
  ')"

# --retry-all-errors (not just --retry-connrefused) because the connect
# failures actually seen live in this cluster ("Failed to connect ... after
# 3061 ms: Could not connect to server") are plain connect timeouts, not
# ECONNREFUSED - --retry-connrefused alone never retries those. Failure here
# is intentionally non-fatal to the step (if/then, not a bare command under
# set -e) - same "skip, don't fail the pipeline" stance as every other guard
# above in this script: this is a best-effort notification side-channel, not
# a pipeline gate, and this Task runs from a Pipeline `finally` block where a
# failed TaskRun fails the whole PipelineRun.
if ! curl --fail --silent --show-error --max-time 10 \
  --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-connrefused \
  -X POST "${WEBHOOK_URL}" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "${payload}"; then
  echo "warn: POST to Slack webhook failed after retries - skipping, not failing the pipeline" >&2
fi

steps.name: notify-backstage
steps.script:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
CFG="${CONFIG_JSON}"
if [[ -n "${CONFIG_JSON_B64}" ]]; then
  CFG="$(base64 -d <<<"${CONFIG_JSON_B64}")"
fi
ENABLED="$(jq -r '.notifications.backstage.enabled // false' <<< "${CFG}")"
if [[ "${ENABLED}" != "true" ]]; then
  echo "backstage notifications disabled in cicd.yaml, skipping"
  exit 0
fi
if [[ -z "${BACKSTAGE_BASE_URL}" ]]; then
  echo "warn: notifications.backstage.enabled=true but backstageBaseUrl is not set on the glidepath-catalog chart - skipping, not failing the pipeline" >&2
  exit 0
fi
TOKEN="$(cat /var/run/secrets/platform/backstage-notify-token 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ -z "${TOKEN}" ]]; then
  echo "warn: notifications.backstage.enabled=true but no glidepath-backstage-notify secret is mounted in this namespace - skipping, not failing the pipeline" >&2
  exit 0
fi

# Tekton's own $(tasks.status) aggregate (what callers pass as STATUS) has no
# "Cancelled" value - a CancelledRunFinally run's finally block still sees
# "Completed" here, same as a normal mixed-result run, since Tekton only
# tracks Succeeded/Failed/Completed/None for that variable. Without this, a
# cancelled build produced a "Build Completed" notification instead of "Build
# Cancelled" (2026-09-16 bug). The PipelineRun's own spec.status is the one
# place cancellation is actually recorded, so read it directly - the same
# kubectl access this script already relies on for the failed-taskrun log
# excerpt below.
PR_SPEC_STATUS="$(kubectl get pipelinerun "${PIPELINE_RUN_NAME}" -n "${APP_NAMESPACE}" -o jsonpath='{.spec.status}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ "${PR_SPEC_STATUS}" == "Cancelled" || "${PR_SPEC_STATUS}" == "CancelledRunFinally" ]]; then
  STATUS="Cancelled"
fi

# Same stage-display vocabulary as notify-slack.yaml - kept identical so the two
# targets read as the same event, not two different notification systems.
case "${STAGE_NAME}" in
  build) STAGE_DISPLAY="Build" ;;
  test) STAGE_DISPLAY="Test" ;;
  deploy) STAGE_DISPLAY="Deploy" ;;
  release) STAGE_DISPLAY="Release" ;;
  deploying) STAGE_DISPLAY="Deploying" ;;
  release-outcome) STAGE_DISPLAY="Release" ;;
  *) STAGE_DISPLAY="${STAGE_NAME}" ;;
esac
# Syncing (the new release-progress-notify mid-flow stage) is routine, not a
# failure - without this it'd render as a "high" severity alert. Cancelled is a
# deliberate user action, not a failure either - it shouldn't read as a red alert.
if [[ "${STATUS}" == "Succeeded" || "${STATUS}" == "Completed" || "${STATUS}" == "Syncing" || "${STATUS}" == "Cancelled" ]]; then
  SEVERITY="normal"
else
  SEVERITY="high"
fi

# The blind "${STAGE_DISPLAY} ${STATUS}" concatenation reads correctly for
# build/test/deploy (STATUS's own Succeeded/Failed vocabulary IS the right
# word there), but not for release's three lifecycle notification points
# (2026-09-14 release-flow redesign): `release` only ever confirms the PR was
# opened/committed, not that anything deployed - a bare "Succeeded" there was
# actively misleading. `release-outcome` (this pipeline's own terminal call) is
# the one place "Succeeded/Failed" is actually true. `deploying`'s STATUS is
# always the single value "Syncing", which "Deploying Syncing" would render
# badly. Env, not app name, leads every one of these three - RecentActivityPanel
# renders this same-app's feed already scoped to one app (Tower is per-app), so
# which ENVIRONMENT a release event is about is the higher-value word to lead
# with; app name stays in the `App:` description line below (still required
# there - useAppNotifications.ts's per-app filter is a free-text search over
# title+description, and this is the one place that still embeds it).
case "${STAGE_NAME}" in
  release)
    if [[ "${STATUS}" == "Succeeded" || "${STATUS}" == "Completed" ]]; then
      TITLE="Release triggered for ${ENV_NAME}"
    else
      TITLE="Release trigger failed for ${ENV_NAME}"
    fi
    ;;
  deploying) TITLE="Deploying release to ${ENV_NAME}" ;;
  release-outcome)
    if [[ "${STATUS}" == "Succeeded" || "${STATUS}" == "Completed" ]]; then
      TITLE="Release succeeded in ${ENV_NAME}"
    else
      TITLE="Release failed in ${ENV_NAME}"
    fi
    ;;
  *) TITLE="${APP_NAME} · ${STAGE_DISPLAY} ${STATUS}" ;;
esac

REPO_SHORT="$(echo "${GIT_URL}" | sed -E 's#https?://github\.com/([^/]+)/([^/.]+).*#\1/\2#')"
SHORT_SHA="${GIT_REVISION:0:12}"

# Tower's own CI/CD tab, not the Tekton Dashboard (2026-09-12: "the
# notifications have a 'View pipeline' link that's currently broken...
# should this link to the CICD tab?") - the Dashboard link this used to
# be (still true of notify-slack.yaml's own identical link) only ever
# resolves with a local port-forward to localhost:9097, dead for
# anyone else viewing the notification. `run` is read by CiCdTab.tsx
# to auto-select this exact PipelineRun on load. Assumes this app's
# catalog Component is named APP_NAME in the default namespace - true
# everywhere onboarding has created one, per this platform's naming
# convention (see glidepathPromote.ts's identical assumption).
RUN_URL="${BACKSTAGE_BASE_URL%/}/tower?entity=component:default/${APP_NAME}&tab=ci-cd&run=${PIPELINE_RUN_NAME}"

# build only - live TaskRun result lookup, not a Tekton result-reference param -
# see notify-slack.yaml's identical block for why (finally tasks are skipped if a
# param references a result from a task that failed/didn't run).
if [[ -z "${IMAGE_REF}" && "${STAGE_NAME}" == "build" ]]; then
  IMAGE_REF="$(kubectl get taskrun -n "${APP_NAMESPACE}" -l "tekton.dev/pipelineRun=${PIPELINE_RUN_NAME},tekton.dev/pipelineTask=build-image" \
    -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.results[?(@.name=="image-ref")].value}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi

pr_url="${PR_URL_PARAM}"
if [[ -z "${pr_url}" && "${STAGE_NAME}" == "release" ]]; then
  pr_url="$(kubectl get taskrun -n "${APP_NAMESPACE}" -l "tekton.dev/pipelineRun=${PIPELINE_RUN_NAME},tekton.dev/pipelineTask=open-release-pr" \
    -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.results[?(@.name=="pr-url")].value}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi

# Failure log excerpt - same non-"Succeeded"/"Completed" trigger and RBAC as
# notify-slack.yaml (pipeline-runner's existing Role already covers this).
log_excerpt=""
if [[ "${STATUS}" != "Succeeded" && "${STATUS}" != "Completed" && "${STATUS}" != "Syncing" ]]; then
  failed_taskrun="$(kubectl get taskrun -n "${APP_NAMESPACE}" -l "tekton.dev/pipelineRun=${PIPELINE_RUN_NAME}" -o json \
    | jq -r '[.items[] | select(.status.conditions[0].status == "False")][0].metadata.name // empty')"
  if [[ -n "${failed_taskrun}" ]]; then
    pod_name="$(kubectl get taskrun "${failed_taskrun}" -n "${APP_NAMESPACE}" -o jsonpath='{.status.podName}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ -n "${pod_name}" ]]; then
      log_excerpt="$(kubectl logs "${pod_name}" -n "${APP_NAMESPACE}" --all-containers --tail=15 2>/dev/null | tail -c 800 || true)"
    fi
    log_excerpt="Failed task: ${failed_taskrun}"$'\n'"${log_excerpt}"
  fi
fi

description="$(printf 'App: %s (%s)\nRepo: %s @ %s\nRun: %s' \
  "${APP_NAME}" "${APP_NAMESPACE}" "${REPO_SHORT}" "${SHORT_SHA}" "${PIPELINE_RUN_NAME}")"
[[ -n "${IMAGE_REF}" ]] && description="${description}"$'\n'"Image: ${IMAGE_REF}"
[[ -n "${ENV_NAME}" ]] && description="${description}"$'\n'"Environment: ${ENV_NAME}"
[[ -n "${pr_url}" ]] && description="${description}"$'\n'"PR: ${pr_url}"
# Chain: correlates this notification with the other release/deploying/
# release-outcome events for the same release - Tower's Recent Activity panel
# parses and strips this line (RecentActivityPanel.tsx/notificationFormatting.tsx),
# it's never meant to be read as prose. Not emitted for non-release stages
# (CHAIN_ID is empty there today - build/test/deploy don't thread chain-id
# through to this Task).
[[ -n "${CHAIN_ID}" ]] && description="${description}"$'\n'"Chain: ${CHAIN_ID}"
[[ -n "${log_excerpt}" ]] && description="${description}"$'\n\n'"${log_excerpt}"

payload="$(jq -n \
  --arg title "${TITLE}" \
  --arg description "${description}" \
  --arg link "${RUN_URL}" \
  --arg severity "${SEVERITY}" \
  --arg topic "${STAGE_NAME}" \
  '{
    recipients: { type: "broadcast" },
    payload: {
      title: $title,
      description: $description,
      link: $link,
      severity: $severity,
      topic: $topic
    }
  }')"

# --retry-all-errors (not just --retry-connrefused) because the connect
# failures actually seen live against backstage.prod.kiac.local ("Failed to
# connect ... after 3061 ms: Could not connect to server") are plain connect
# timeouts, not ECONNREFUSED - --retry-connrefused alone never retries those.
# Failure here is intentionally non-fatal to the step (if/then, not a bare
# command under set -e) - same "skip, don't fail the pipeline" stance as
# every other guard above in this script: this is a best-effort notification
# side-channel, not a pipeline gate, and this Task runs from a Pipeline
# `finally` block where a failed TaskRun fails the whole PipelineRun.
if ! curl --fail --silent --show-error --max-time 10 \
  --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-connrefused \
  -X POST "${BACKSTAGE_BASE_URL%/}/api/notifications" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -d "${payload}"; then
  echo "warn: POST to Backstage notifications API failed after retries - skipping, not failing the pipeline" >&2
fi

steps.name: domain-event
steps.script:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
if [[ "${ONLY_ON_SUCCESS}" == "true" && "${PIPELINE_STATUS}" != "Succeeded" && "${PIPELINE_STATUS}" != "Completed" ]]; then
  echo "not sending ${EVENT_TYPE}: pipeline status is '${PIPELINE_STATUS}' and this event only fires on success"
  exit 0
fi
# base64 overrides (see the params' descriptions) are decoded before cdevents.sh is
# sourced, since it reads PLATFORM_CONFIG_JSON from the environment.
if [[ -n "${PLATFORM_CONFIG_JSON_B64}" ]]; then
  PLATFORM_CONFIG_JSON="$(base64 -d <<<"${PLATFORM_CONFIG_JSON_B64}")"
  export PLATFORM_CONFIG_JSON
fi
source "${PLATFORM_LIB}/cdevents.sh"

content="${SUBJECT_CONTENT_JSON}"
if [[ -n "${SUBJECT_CONTENT_JSON_B64}" ]]; then
  content="$(base64 -d <<<"${SUBJECT_CONTENT_JSON_B64}")"
fi
if [[ -n "${TEKTON_STATUS}" ]]; then
  outcome="$(cdevents_map_outcome "${TEKTON_STATUS}")"
  content="$(jq -c --arg o "${outcome}" '. + {outcome: $o}' <<<"${content}")"
fi

cdevent_send "${EVENT_TYPE}" "${SUBJECT_TYPE}" "${TEKTON_PIPELINE_RUN}" "${content}"

steps.name: verdict
steps.script:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail
failed=()
check() { local code; code="$(cat "$2" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"; [[ "${code}" == "0" ]] || failed+=("$1 (exit ${code})"); }
check resolve "/tekton/steps/step-resolve/exitCode"
check end-stage-span "/tekton/steps/step-end-stage-span/exitCode"
check end-flow "/tekton/steps/step-end-flow/exitCode"
check notify-slack "/tekton/steps/step-notify-slack/exitCode"
check notify-backstage "/tekton/steps/step-notify-backstage/exitCode"
check domain-event "/tekton/steps/step-domain-event/exitCode"

steps.name: resolve-build-config
steps.script:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
CFG='{"apiVersion":"platform/v1","kind":"PipelineConfig","build":{"agent":"python-3.12","unitTest":{"enabled":false,"command":"./test.sh"},"containerfile":"./Containerfile","platforms":["arm64","amd64"],"artifacts":[],"sonar":false,"cache":{"enabled":false,"size":"small"},"sourceVolume":{"size":"small"}},"pipelines":{"ci":{"trigger":{"source":"git","event":"push","branch":"main"},"steps":[{"stage":"build"},{"stage":"deploy","env":"dev"}]}},"deploy":{"strategy":"rollout","environments":[{"name":"dev","tier":"ground"}],"releaseFile":"glidepath/releases/{env}.yaml","target":"k8s-rollout","chart":{},"ecs":{"region":"us-east-1"},"lambda":{"region":"us-east-1"},"azureContainerApps":{}},"notifications":{"backstage":{"enabled":true},"slack":{"enabled":false,"scanResults":true}},"test":{"enabled":true},"ephemeralEnvironments":{"branch":{"enabled":false,"patterns":["preview/*"]},"pullRequest":{"enabled":false,"labels":["preview"]},"ttl":"5d"},"governance":{"sast":false,"imageScan":false,"policyCheck":false,"sbom":false,"allowedCommitSigners":[]},"secrets":[]}'
# build.dockerfile renamed build.containerfile 2026-09-22 (schemas/
# cicd.schema.json - "Containerfile" is this platform's deliberate,
# vendor-neutral term for the same file). The `// "./Containerfile"`
# here is defense-in-depth, not the only guard: validate-cicd-config
# now applies every schema default (including this one) onto
# config-json centrally before any Task sees it - see that Task's own
# comment for the real bug this used to be (a missing key handed
# kaniko a literal ".../null" path) before that central fix existed.
CONTAINERFILE_PATH="$(jq -r '.build.containerfile // "./Containerfile"' <<< "${CFG}")"
SHORT_SHA="$(cut -c1-7 <<< "5225f67d24effefc3fea606fbce0ac18dc80734c")"
SRC="/workspace/source"

# Version selection: a tag push is authoritative - use it directly, same as the
# old cd-pipelines platform's task-get-tag.yaml. Any other trigger derives the
# version from the app repo's own manifest instead of a fixed placeholder, so
# dev/main-branch images carry a real, traceable version rather than always
# "0.0.0" - same manifest lookup + precedence order (package.json before
# pom.xml) as that same prior Task.
GIT_TAG=''
if [[ -n "${GIT_TAG}" ]]; then
  # PaC provides refs/tags/v1.2.3 or refs/tags/v1.2.3-rc.1
  # Extract: 1.2.3 or 1.2.3-rc.1 (remove refs/tags/ and leading 'v' if present)
  VERSION=$(echo "${GIT_TAG}" | sed -E 's|^refs/tags/v?||')
elif [[ -f "${SRC}/package.json" ]]; then
  VERSION="$(jq -r '.version' "${SRC}/package.json")"
elif [[ -f "${SRC}/pom.xml" ]]; then
  VERSION="$(xmllint --xpath '/*[local-name()="project"]/*[local-name()="version"]/text()' "${SRC}/pom.xml" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  # Maven's CI-friendly-versions pattern (<version>${revision}</version>, the
  # real value under <properties><revision>) - same fallback task-get-tag.yaml
  # used, since a literal "${revision}" string is not a usable image tag.
  if [[ "${VERSION}" == '${revision}' ]]; then
    VERSION="$(xmllint --xpath '/*[local-name()="project"]/*[local-name()="properties"]/*[local-name()="revision"]/text()' "${SRC}/pom.xml" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  fi
  VERSION="${VERSION%%-*}"
elif [[ -f "${SRC}/pyproject.toml" ]]; then
  # A Python app had no manifest this precedence chain read at all - every image
  # came out "0.0.0-<sha>" regardless of what pyproject.toml actually declared
  # (found live on baggage-api/boarding-api/flight-api - known-gap #1). yq (already
  # in the toolbox, v4.44.3) reads TOML natively via -p toml; "null" is yq's own
  # string for a genuinely absent key (not the possibly-templated `${revision}`
  # placeholder pom.xml's block guards against - PEP 621's [project.version] is a
  # plain literal, no dynamic-version convention to special-case here).
  VERSION="$(yq -p toml -r '.project.version // ""' "${SRC}/pyproject.toml" 2>/dev/null || true)"
elif [[ -f "${SRC}/VERSION" ]]; then
  # Generic escape hatch for a repo using none of the three manifests above -
  # a single line, no key to extract, just trim whitespace/newline.
  VERSION="$(tr -d '[:space:]' < "${SRC}/VERSION")"
fi
[[ -z "${VERSION:-}" ]] && VERSION="0.0.0"

if [[ "false" == "true" ]]; then
  # 12-char sha, matching glidepath-app's ephemeral-envs.yaml, which
  # computes this same image reference independently via ArgoCD's own template
  # (trunc-12'd .head_sha - see that file's own comment).
  IMAGE_REF="ghcr.io/jfillman/flight-attendant:$(cut -c1-12 <<< "5225f67d24effefc3fea606fbce0ac18dc80734c")"
else
  IMAGE_REF="ghcr.io/jfillman/flight-attendant:${VERSION}-${SHORT_SHA}"
fi
# Defaults to both platforms when build.platforms is omitted entirely, matching
# schemas/cicd.schema.json's own default - jq's `// ["arm64","amd64"]` only
# kicks in when the key is absent/null, not when it's an explicit (possibly
# single-element) array, so an app that sets platforms: [amd64] gets exactly
# that, not both.
# `|| true` on each: jq -e exits non-zero for a legitimate "false" match (the
# platform genuinely isn't requested), which under this script's `set -e` would
# otherwise abort the whole step - not an error case, so it must not fail the build.
BUILD_ARM64="false"
BUILD_AMD64="false"
jq -e '(.build.platforms // ["arm64","amd64"]) | index("arm64") != null' <<< "${CFG}" >/dev/null && BUILD_ARM64="true" || true
jq -e '(.build.platforms // ["arm64","amd64"]) | index("amd64") != null' <<< "${CFG}" >/dev/null && BUILD_AMD64="true" || true

echo -n "${CONTAINERFILE_PATH}" | tee "/tekton/steps/step-resolve-build-config/results/containerfile-path"
echo -n "${IMAGE_REF}" | tee "/tekton/steps/step-resolve-build-config/results/image-ref"
echo -n "${VERSION}" | tee "/tekton/steps/step-resolve-build-config/results/version"
echo -n "${BUILD_ARM64}" | tee "/tekton/steps/step-resolve-build-config/results/build-arm64"
echo -n "${BUILD_AMD64}" | tee "/tekton/steps/step-resolve-build-config/results/build-amd64"
# -n here matters, unlike the two lines above it's not just style: this result is
# read back by emit-image-ref-and-span via a cross-step env var substitution, not a
# `cat`-based one - command substitution strips a trailing newline automatically,
# a raw env var substitution doesn't. A bare `date | tee` here left one in, which
# otel-cli's --start flag received literally - a real bug, found live: the span
# silently never reached Tempo (no error, no exit-nonzero, just absent).
echo -n "$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%NZ")" | tee "/tekton/steps/step-resolve-build-config/results/span-start-time"

results.name: version
results.description: Resolved VERSION alone (no -<sha> suffix) - exists so build-and-push-{arm64,amd64} can set org.opencontainers.image.version without re-parsing it back out of image-ref.

results.name: build-arm64
results.description: "true"/"false" - whether cicd.yaml's build.platforms includes arm64 (default: both platforms, so default is "true").

results.name: build-amd64
results.description: "true"/"false" - same as build-arm64, for amd64.

results.name: span-start-time
results.description: Stamped immediately before kaniko starts - see emit-image-ref-and-span's span-emission comment for why the actual span is sent from there instead of here.

steps.name: build-and-push-arm64
steps.script:
#!/busybox/sh
set -eu
if [ "${BUILD_ARM64}" != "true" ]; then
  echo "arm64 not in this app's cicd.yaml build.platforms - skipping"
  exit 0
fi
exec /kaniko/executor \
  --dockerfile=/workspace/source/${CONTAINERFILE_PATH} \
  --context=/workspace/source \
  --destination=${IMAGE_REF}-arm64 \
  --custom-platform=linux/arm64 \
  --cache=true \
  --cache-ttl=336h \
  --label=org.opencontainers.image.version=${OCI_VERSION} \
  --label=org.opencontainers.image.revision=${OCI_REVISION} \
  --label=org.opencontainers.image.source=${OCI_SOURCE} \
  --label=org.opencontainers.image.created=${OCI_CREATED} \
  --build-arg=HANGAR_VERSION=${OCI_VERSION} \
  --build-arg=HANGAR_GIT_REVISION=${OCI_REVISION}

steps.script:
#!/busybox/sh
set -eu
if [ "${BUILD_AMD64}" != "true" ]; then
  echo "amd64 not in this app's cicd.yaml build.platforms - skipping"
  exit 0
fi
exec /kaniko/executor \
  --dockerfile=/workspace/source/${CONTAINERFILE_PATH} \
  --context=/workspace/source \
  --destination=${IMAGE_REF}-amd64 \
  --custom-platform=linux/amd64 \
  --cache=true \
  --cache-ttl=336h \
  --label=org.opencontainers.image.version=${OCI_VERSION} \
  --label=org.opencontainers.image.revision=${OCI_REVISION} \
  --label=org.opencontainers.image.source=${OCI_SOURCE} \
  --label=org.opencontainers.image.created=${OCI_CREATED} \
  --build-arg=HANGAR_VERSION=${OCI_VERSION} \
  --build-arg=HANGAR_GIT_REVISION=${OCI_REVISION}

steps.name: publish-multiarch-manifest
steps.script:
#!/busybox/sh
set -eu
if [ "${BUILD_ARM64}" = "true" ] && [ "${BUILD_AMD64}" = "true" ]; then
  crane index append \
    -m "${IMAGE_REF}-arm64" \
    -m "${IMAGE_REF}-amd64" \
    -t "${IMAGE_REF}"
elif [ "${BUILD_ARM64}" = "true" ]; then
  crane cp "${IMAGE_REF}-arm64" "${IMAGE_REF}"
elif [ "${BUILD_AMD64}" = "true" ]; then
  crane cp "${IMAGE_REF}-amd64" "${IMAGE_REF}"
else
  echo "error: build.platforms resolved to an empty set - schema's minItems:1 should have caught this at validate-cicd-config. Refusing to publish nothing." >&2
  exit 1
fi

crane digest "${IMAGE_REF}" | tr -d '\n' | tee "/tekton/results/image-digest"

steps.name: emit-image-ref-and-span
steps.script:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
source "${PLATFORM_LIB}/otel.sh"
echo -n "${IMAGE_REF}" | tee "/tekton/results/image-ref"
echo -n "${IMAGE_REPO}" | tee "/tekton/results/image-repo"
echo -n "${VERSION}" | tee "/tekton/results/version"
echo -n "${IMAGE_REPO}" | tee "/tekton/results/IMAGE_URL"
# image-digest is a TASK-level result (publish-multiarch-manifest writes it via
# `crane digest`, now that this Task builds multi-arch - see that step's own
# comment), not a step-level one - a cross-step "steps dot results dot name" env
# var reference only
# applies to step-scoped results and silently resolves to the literal unresolved
# placeholder string for a task-level one (confirmed live, a real bug on the first
# attempt - and note: writing that exact syntax even inside a comment here trips
# Tekton's admission webhook, since its variable substitution is a plain string
# match with no awareness of bash comments - confirmed live the hard way). A
# results-dot-name-dot-path reference inline in script is ALSO rejected once the
# result belongs to an earlier step. Task-level result files live at the
# well-documented, stable /tekton/results/<name> path regardless of which step
# wrote them, so read it directly rather than fighting either restriction.
cat /tekton/results/image-digest | tee "/tekton/results/IMAGE_DIGEST"
otel_task_span_send "build-image" "${FLOW_TRACEPARENT}" "${STAGE_SPAN_ID}" \
  "${SPAN_START}" "$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%NZ")" "Succeeded"

params.name: config-json
params.description: Output of validate-cicd-config's config-json result.

params.name: image-repo
params.description: Destination registry/repo, e.g. ghcr.io/<org>/<app>.

params.name: git-tag
params.description: Git tag from PaC (e.g., refs/tags/v1.2.3). Used to extract version for image tag. Empty for branch-based triggers.

params.name: git-url
params.description: App repo URL, already threaded through build.yaml's own git-url param - only consumed here for the org.opencontainers.image.source label below. Defaulted (not required) so this Task doesn't newly reject a hand-built TaskRun that omits it; an empty source label is harmless.

params.name: pr-tag-only
params.description: "true" tags the image as <12-char-sha> alone, skipping the <version>-<short-sha> scheme below entirely. Set by deliver-onboarding-files.yaml for pull_request-triggered flows only - a PR's package.json version isn't something ArgoCD's pullRequest generator can read at manifest-generation time (glidepath-app's ephemeral-envs.yaml computes this exact image reference independently, from .head_sha alone, to know what to deploy), so PR images need a tag ephemeral-envs.yaml can predict without it.

params.name: flow-traceparent
params.description: Root traceparent for the whole flow (from start-flow-root-span) - gives the kaniko-duration span its trace id. See emit-image-ref-and-span's own span-emission comment for why this Task can't wrap kaniko directly.

params.name: stage-span-id
params.description: The current stage's own span id (from start-stage-span) - the kaniko-duration span is parented to it.

results.name: version
results.description: Task-level copy of resolve-build-config's own version step-result - exists so a downstream Task (e.g. build-artifact.yaml, publishing a wheel/binary from the same build) can reference $(tasks.build-image.results.version) directly instead of re-deriving VERSION itself and risking drift from the image tag.

results.name: image-repo
results.description: Bare repo name, no tag - only exists so build.yaml's Pipeline-level IMAGE_URL result (Tekton Chains' type-hinting convention, see docs/image-signing.md) has a task-result expression to reference; Tekton's admission webhook rejects a Pipeline result whose value is a plain $(params.*) reference, it must be $(tasks.*.results.*).

results.name: IMAGE_URL
results.description: Same value as image-repo, duplicated under Conforma's exact-cased Task-level type-hint name - policy/release/lib/tekton/task_results.rego's build_tasks() looks for a task with results *ending in* "IMAGE_URL"/"IMAGE_DIGEST", independent of and unrelated to Chains' own artifacts.taskrun.storage signing/storage config (confirmed live before adding this - it only reads predicate.buildConfig.tasks[].results, which Chains already populates for every task regardless of storage settings). See docs/provenance-policy.md.

results.name: IMAGE_DIGEST
results.description: Same value as image-digest, duplicated under Conforma's exact-cased Task-level type-hint name - see IMAGE_URL above.

steps.name: prepare
steps.script:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

### 1. Flow and stage ids - was start-flow-root-span.yaml's check-and-start step
### plus otel-stage-span-start's one-liner. Idempotent: an incoming chain-id
### (event-chained) is passed through with its traceparent/start-time; an empty
### one (flow root) mints all three. The stage span is a sibling under the flow
### root, never nested - see docs/admin/tracing.md.
source "${PLATFORM_LIB}/otel.sh"
# Not cdevents.sh - that file hard-requires CDEVENTS_BROKER_URL/NAMESPACE/
# TEKTON_PIPELINE_RUN to even source; chain-slug.sh is the same
# chain_id_to_slug function with no such requirement.
source "${PLATFORM_LIB}/chain-slug.sh"

if [[ -n "${INCOMING_CHAIN_ID}" ]]; then
  chain_id="${INCOMING_CHAIN_ID}"
  printf '%s' "${INCOMING_TRACEPARENT}" > "/tekton/results/traceparent"
  printf '%s' "${INCOMING_FLOW_START_TIME}" > "/tekton/results/start-time"
  printf '%s' "${chain_id}" > "/tekton/results/chain-id"
else
  read -r traceparent start_time <<< "$(otel_flow_root_begin)"
  printf '%s' "${traceparent}" > "/tekton/results/traceparent"
  printf '%s' "${start_time}" > "/tekton/results/start-time"
  # printf, not `uuidgen | tee` - uuidgen's trailing newline once landed in the
  # result verbatim and broke otel-cli's CSV-based --attrs parser downstream
  # (platform.stage silently dropped from every stage span, caught in Tempo).
  chain_id="$(uuidgen)"
  printf '%s' "${chain_id}" > "/tekton/results/chain-id"
fi
# A pure function of chain-id - always the same word pair a downstream
# CDEvent-triggered stage's own PipelineRun name derives for this chain.
printf '%s' "$(chain_id_to_slug "${chain_id}")" > "/tekton/results/chain-slug"

# This stage's own span: fail fast here if the traceparent is malformed rather
# than only at send time in stage-debrief, much later.
read -r span_id stage_start_time <<< "$(otel_stage_span_begin "$(cat "/tekton/results/traceparent")")"
printf '%s' "${span_id}" > "/tekton/results/span-id"
printf '%s' "${stage_start_time}" > "/tekton/results/stage-start-time"

### 2. pipelinerun.started - was a send-cdevent TaskRun. Same lib call the
### cdevent-send StepAction makes; cdevents.sh reads the PLATFORM_* values from
### the environment. Its token path is a plain variable, overridden after sourcing
### because the GitHub-App token already occupies /var/run/secrets/platform here.
### No error handling on purpose, same as the TaskRun it replaces: a broker that
### rejects the announcement fails the stage early rather than letting it run
### unannounced.
export PLATFORM_CHAIN_ID="$(cat "/tekton/results/chain-id")"
export PLATFORM_TRACEPARENT="$(cat "/tekton/results/traceparent")"
export PLATFORM_FLOW_START_TIME="$(cat "/tekton/results/start-time")"
source "${PLATFORM_LIB}/cdevents.sh"
_BROKER_TOKEN_PATH=/var/run/secrets/platform-broker/broker-token
cdevent_send "dev.cdevents.pipelinerun.started.0.3.0" "pipelineRun" "${TEKTON_PIPELINE_RUN}" "{\"pipelineName\": \"${STAGE_NAME}\"}"
echo

### 3. Clone - was clone-repo-authenticated.yaml. Only when the `source`
### workspace is bound (build/test always; a git-rooted deploy/release). A fresh,
### single-repo-scoped GitHub App installation token per run
### (catalog/lib/github-app.sh), proven by this pod's own ServiceAccount identity,
### so it works identically whether PaC or the broker created the PipelineRun.
if [[ "true" == "true" ]]; then
  source "${PLATFORM_LIB}/github-app.sh"

owner="$(echo "${GIT_URL}" | sed -E 's#https?://github\.com/([^/]+)/.*#\1#')"
token="$(github_app_installation_token "${owner}" "${APP_NAME}")"
clone_url="https://x-access-token:${token}@github.com/${owner}/${APP_NAME}.git"

cd "/workspace/source"
# Workspace volume is owned by a different uid than this step runs as - git
# refuses to operate at all otherwise ("detected dubious ownership").
git config --global --add safe.directory "/workspace/source"
git init --quiet
git remote add origin "${clone_url}"
git fetch --quiet --depth=1 origin "${GIT_REVISION}"
git checkout --quiet FETCH_HEAD

echo -n "${GIT_URL}" | tee "/tekton/results/url"
git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD | tr -d '\n' | tee "/tekton/results/commit"
  echo
else
  echo "no source workspace bound (event-chained ${STAGE_NAME}) - nothing to clone"
  printf '' > "/tekton/results/url"
  printf '' > "/tekton/results/commit"
fi

### 4. cicd.yaml -> config-json - was validate-cicd-config.yaml, unchanged for a
### bound workspace: read fresh from the triggering commit, schema-validated
### (schemas/cicd.schema.json, baked into the toolbox image), every default
### applied, the most-used fields extracted. For an unbound workspace the
### inherited config-json - already validated and defaulted upstream - is passed
### through; that is what resolve-notify-config used to do, minus its own
### best-effort git-rooted clone (step 3 covers that now, with real validation).
CONFIG_FILE="/workspace/source/cicd.yaml"

if [[ "true" == "true" ]]; then
  if [[ ! -f "${CONFIG_FILE}" ]]; then
    echo "error: ${CONFIG_FILE} not found." >&2
    echo "Every app repo needs a cicd.yaml at its root - see docs/user-guide/cicd-yaml-reference.md" >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  yq -o=json '.' "${CONFIG_FILE}" > /tmp/cicd.json

  # The pre-ADR-0019 environment keys were removed 2026-10-07; say what replaced
  # them instead of yajsv's bare "additional property not allowed".
  old_keys="$(jq -r '(.deploy // {}) | [keys[] | select(. == "lowerEnvironments" or . == "upperEnvironments" or . == "promotionOrder")] | join(", ")' /tmp/cicd.json)"
  if [[ -n "${old_keys}" ]]; then
    echo "error: cicd.yaml sets deploy.${old_keys}, which deploy.environments replaced (list each environment once, in promotion order, with tier: ground or flight; see docs/user/cicd-yaml-reference.md)." >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  if ! yajsv -s /opt/platform/schemas/cicd.schema.json /tmp/cicd.json; then
    echo "" >&2
    echo "error: cicd.yaml failed schema validation (see above)." >&2
    echo "Reference: docs/user-guide/cicd-yaml-reference.md" >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  # Applies every schemas/cicd.schema.json "default" the developer's cicd.yaml
  # left unset, recursively, so config-json is always a COMPLETE document - a
  # Task never sees an absent key for a field the schema says has a default.
  # (build.containerfile once reached kaniko as the literal ".../null" path
  # because a Task's own `// default` was missing - applying defaults once,
  # centrally, closes that whole bug class.) Only walks `properties`;
  # `pipelines`' dynamic per-flow-name keys have no schema defaults.
  # (heredoc terminators below sit at column 0 - bash requires it even inside this if-block)
  cat > /tmp/apply-defaults.jq <<'JQ_PROGRAM'
  def apply_defaults(schema):
    if (schema.type == "object") and (schema.properties != null) then
      . as $obj
      | reduce (schema.properties | to_entries[]) as $e
          ( $obj;
            ($e.key) as $k | ($e.value) as $s
            | (.[$k]) as $cur
            | if ($cur == null) then
                if ($s.type == "object" and $s.properties != null) then
                  .[$k] = ({} | apply_defaults($s))
                elif ($s.default != null) then
                  .[$k] = $s.default
                else
                  .
                end
              else
                .[$k] = ($cur | apply_defaults($s))
              end
          )
    else
      .
    end;
  apply_defaults($schema)
JQ_PROGRAM
  jq --argjson schema "$(cat /opt/platform/schemas/cicd.schema.json)" \
    -f /tmp/apply-defaults.jq /tmp/cicd.json > /tmp/cicd-defaulted.json

  # Environments (ADR-0019): deploy.environments, or one Ground environment, dev, when it is unset.
  cat > /tmp/normalize-envs.jq <<'JQ_NORMALIZE'
  .deploy.environments = ($orig.deploy.environments // [{name: "dev", tier: "ground"}])
JQ_NORMALIZE
  jq --argjson orig "$(cat /tmp/cicd.json)" -f /tmp/normalize-envs.jq /tmp/cicd-defaulted.json > /tmp/cicd-normalized.json
  mv /tmp/cicd-normalized.json /tmp/cicd-defaulted.json
  echo "cicd.yaml is valid."
else
  # Event-chained: the upstream stage already validated and defaulted this.
  printf '%s' "${INCOMING_CONFIG_JSON}" > /tmp/cicd-defaulted.json
  if ! jq -e 'type == "object"' /tmp/cicd-defaulted.json >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "warning: inherited config-json is not a JSON object - using {} (notifications and target resolution will see an empty config)" >&2
    printf '{}' > /tmp/cicd-defaulted.json
  fi
  echo "no source workspace bound - passing the inherited config-json through ($(wc -c < /tmp/cicd-defaulted.json) bytes)"
fi

# Compact, not pretty-printed: see this file's header on the kubelet's per-container
# termination-message budget. Every consumer reads it with jq, so whitespace is noise.
jq -c . /tmp/cicd-defaulted.json | tr -d '\n' > "/tekton/results/config-json"

# Flag extraction - echo -n, never a bare `jq -r | tee`: jq's trailing newline
# once landed in a result and broke Tekton's exact-string `when:` gates.
# `if == true` rather than `// false`: jq's `//` treats false like null.
flag() { jq -r "if ($1) == true then \"true\" else \"false\" end" /tmp/cicd-defaulted.json; }
echo -n "$(jq -r 'if .build.script != null and .build.script != "" then "true" else "false" end' /tmp/cicd-defaulted.json)" | tee "/tekton/results/has-build-script" > /dev/null
echo -n "$(flag .governance.sast)" | tee "/tekton/results/sast" > /dev/null
echo -n "$(flag .governance.imageScan)" | tee "/tekton/results/image-scan" > /dev/null
echo -n "$(flag .governance.policyCheck)" | tee "/tekton/results/policy-check" > /dev/null
echo -n "$(flag .governance.sbom)" | tee "/tekton/results/sbom" > /dev/null
echo -n "$(jq -r '(.build.artifacts // []) | index("python-wheel") != null' /tmp/cicd-defaulted.json)" | tee "/tekton/results/artifacts-python-wheel" > /dev/null
echo -n "$(jq -r '(.build.artifacts // []) | index("go-binary") != null' /tmp/cicd-defaulted.json)" | tee "/tekton/results/artifacts-go-binary" > /dev/null

# build.agent -> image via build-agents.env (formerly resolve-build-agent-image's
# own step). Only an error when a cicd.yaml was actually validated above - an
# event-chained deploy/release never needs the agent image.
AGENT="$(jq -r '.build.agent // ""' /tmp/cicd-defaulted.json)"
AGENT_IMAGE=""
if [[ -n "${AGENT}" ]]; then
  AGENT_IMAGE="$(grep -E "^${AGENT}=" /opt/platform/lib/build-agents.env | cut -d= -f2- || true)"
  if [[ -z "${AGENT_IMAGE}" && "true" == "true" ]]; then
    echo "error: build.agent '${AGENT}' has no entry in build-agents.env - this should be impossible if schema validation passed, file a platform bug." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi
echo -n "${AGENT_IMAGE}" | tee "/tekton/results/agent-image" > /dev/null

steps.name: resolve-test-command
steps.script:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
CFG='{"apiVersion":"platform/v1","kind":"PipelineConfig","build":{"agent":"python-3.12","unitTest":{"enabled":false,"command":"./test.sh"},"containerfile":"./Containerfile","platforms":["arm64","amd64"],"artifacts":[],"sonar":false,"cache":{"enabled":false,"size":"small"},"sourceVolume":{"size":"small"}},"pipelines":{"ci":{"trigger":{"source":"git","event":"push","branch":"main"},"steps":[{"stage":"build"},{"stage":"deploy","env":"dev"}]}},"deploy":{"strategy":"rollout","environments":[{"name":"dev","tier":"ground"}],"releaseFile":"glidepath/releases/{env}.yaml","target":"k8s-rollout","chart":{},"ecs":{"region":"us-east-1"},"lambda":{"region":"us-east-1"},"azureContainerApps":{}},"notifications":{"backstage":{"enabled":true},"slack":{"enabled":false,"scanResults":true}},"test":{"enabled":true},"ephemeralEnvironments":{"branch":{"enabled":false,"patterns":["preview/*"]},"pullRequest":{"enabled":false,"labels":["preview"]},"ttl":"5d"},"governance":{"sast":false,"imageScan":false,"policyCheck":false,"sbom":false,"allowedCommitSigners":[]},"secrets":[]}'
# NOT `.build.unitTest.enabled // true` - a real, previously-undiscovered bug
# found live (see docs/user-guide/cicd-yaml-reference.md's own writeup): jq's `//` operator
# treats `false` the same as `null`/missing and falls through to the default, so
# an explicit `unitTest.enabled: false` was silently ignored, always resolving to
# "true" - no Application has ever actually been able to disable unit tests via
# cicd.yaml. `if == false then false else true end` is the correct way to give a
# boolean field a true default while still respecting an explicit false.
ENABLED="$(jq -r 'if .build.unitTest.enabled == false then "false" else "true" end' <<< "${CFG}")"
CMD="$(jq -r '.build.unitTest.command // "./test.sh"' <<< "${CFG}")"
echo -n "${ENABLED}" | tee "/tekton/steps/step-resolve-test-command/results/enabled"
echo -n "${CMD}" | tee "/tekton/steps/step-resolve-test-command/results/command"

# Mirrors build-source.yaml's detection so test.sh's own `npm ci`/`yarn install`
# reuses the tarballs build.sh just fetched (or vice versa - the two run
# concurrently, and both caches are safe for concurrent access). Kept inline
# rather than in catalog/lib because that would need a toolbox image rebuild for
# a four-line case statement.
CACHE_TYPE=""
if [[ "$(jq -r '.build.cache.enabled // false' <<< "${CFG}")" == "true" ]]; then
  case "$(jq -r '.build.agent' <<< "${CFG}")" in
    nodejs-*)
      if [[ -f "/workspace/source/yarn.lock" && ! -f "/workspace/source/package-lock.json" ]]; then
        CACHE_TYPE="yarn"
      else
        CACHE_TYPE="npm"
      fi
      ;;
  esac
fi
echo -n "${CACHE_TYPE}" | tee "/tekton/steps/step-resolve-test-command/results/cache-type"

results.name: cache-type
results.description: 'npm'/'yarn'/'' - the dependency cache the unit-test step should point its package manager at. Same detection as build-source.yaml's resolve-build-script-path (agent prefix + lockfile), minus Maven: its local repository isn't safe for concurrent writers and build-source runs concurrently with this Task, so sharing it would mean serializing tests behind the build. Empty when build.cache.enabled is false or the agent has no cache support.

steps.name: unit-test
steps.script:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
mkdir -p /tmp/test-src
cp -a "${SOURCE_WORKSPACE}/." /tmp/test-src/
rm -rf /tmp/test-src/node_modules
# Same directory layout and env vars as build-source.yaml's run-build-script step
# (/cache/<tool>) so the two steps share one download cache per app. Only the
# package manager's cache location changes - test.sh still owns its own install.
if [[ -n "${CACHE_TYPE}" ]]; then
  CACHE_DIR="/cache/${CACHE_TYPE}"
  mkdir -p "${CACHE_DIR}"
  case "${CACHE_TYPE}" in
    npm) export NPM_CONFIG_CACHE="${CACHE_DIR}" ;;
    yarn)
      export YARN_CACHE_FOLDER="${CACHE_DIR}"
      export YARN_GLOBAL_FOLDER="${CACHE_DIR}"
      export YARN_ENABLE_GLOBAL_CACHE=true
      ;;
  esac
  echo "build.cache: unit-test sharing the ${CACHE_TYPE} download cache at ${CACHE_DIR}"
fi
# Plain `date`, not catalog/lib/otel.sh - this step runs inside the app's own
# resolved build-agent image, which has neither otel-cli nor $PLATFORM_LIB. See
# build-source.yaml's own run-build-script step for the full rationale - same
# handoff-to-a-later-toolbox-step pattern.
date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%NZ" | tee "/tekton/results/span-start-time"
if [[ "${TEST_ENABLED}" != "true" ]]; then
  echo "unit tests disabled in cicd.yaml, skipping"
  echo -n "skipped" | tee "/tekton/results/outcome"
else
  # set +e here, not the whole script: `outcome`/span-end-time must still be
  # written on a real test failure - same "onError: continue, capture the
  # exit code, re-raise it explicitly at the end" pattern
  # catalog/tasks/sast-scan.yaml/image-scan.yaml already use, applied at the
  # script level here instead since this step has no onError of its own.
  set +e
  bash -c "${TEST_COMMAND}"
  TEST_EXIT_CODE=$?
  set -e
  if [[ "${TEST_EXIT_CODE}" -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo -n "passed" | tee "/tekton/results/outcome"
  else
    echo -n "failed" | tee "/tekton/results/outcome"
  fi
fi
date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%NZ" | tee "/tekton/results/span-end-time"
if [[ "${TEST_EXIT_CODE:-0}" -ne 0 ]]; then
  exit "${TEST_EXIT_CODE}"
fi
